reader.requirement: An implementor-defined unsuccessful condition on a sequential file must set I-O status 9x, with x the implementor's, and the condition must not duplicate any condition that values 00 through 49 specify in 1985.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.FileSharingFacility (2002+): at 85 no file lock is taken and no '61' file-sharing status is produced; a second connector's OPEN of the same file answers '00'
a host refusal of the OPEN answers '61' when the sharing facility is in effect and the 1985 value '30' at 85
the clause-less connector's sharing mode: no restriction at 85 (FileSharing.AllOther)
the file-sharing-facility row (introduced 2002) the three sites above read
ORGANIZATION LINE SEQUENTIAL refused below 2023 (COBOL0900), so the line-sequential '71' cannot arise at 85
ASSIGN USING refused below 2002 (COBOL0900), so the '31' association failure cannot arise at 85

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 2002 and later a second connector's conflicting OPEN answers '61' (and a host refusal '61'); at 85 the file sharing facility is off, so those OPENs answer '00' or the 1985 '30', and no status outside the 1985 list or 9x is produced for a sequential file

reader.notes: Both implementor values are 9x: '90' for a LINAGE page size or footing value not greater than zero or a footing past the page size, a condition no 1985 value 00-49 names, and '91' for an unrepresentable record character, which is not the 1985 '30' (no further information) or a 4x logic error. The probes show the conditions 1985 does name keep their own values at 85 (35, 42, 44, 47) and no 9x stands in for them.
reader.at-2023: ios7 at 2023: 91 the same; ios2 at 2023: the second OPEN of one file answers 61 (the 2002 facility)

refuter.evidence: Same probe io6.cob at --std 85: after the LINAGE-0 OPEN OUTPUT answers 90, a WRITE answers 90 and a CLOSE 00. Under 1985 that OPEN was unsuccessful (9x is 'Implementor-Defined Condition With Unsuccessful Completion'; §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR1: only a successful OPEN results in an open mode), so the WRITE is a WRITE on a file not open in output mode, the condition 48 names (§1985:VII.1.3.5 GRL2.4), and the 1985 LINAGE values are only determined at OPEN and page overflow on an open file (§1985:VII.3.7.4 GR6). Answering 90 there reports, under the implementor's 9x, a condition that 00-49 already specify; the CLOSE answering 00 instead of 42 is the same root. cite.py: OK §1985:VII.1.3.5 GRL2.5 ["This condition must not duplicate any condition specified by the I-O status values 00 through 49"]; OK §1985:VII.1.3.5 GRL2.4 (41/42). The value choice itself (90 for LINAGE, 91 for a character with no byte image) and the absence of 61/51/31/71 at 85 (reader's ios probes; my io1-io3: 30/35/37 only) hold. Reading stated: an unsuccessful OPEN leaves no open mode at 1985, so the 90 latch on later WRITEs stands in for 48. kb/Work: none for 1985 (PB526 chose the 2023 continuation for all editions).

refuter.corrected: NON-CONFORMING (misleads-diagnosis; cause a). The 9x LINAGE condition at 1985 must leave the OPEN unsuccessful, so a later WRITE answers 48 and CLOSE 42 (1985 conditions 00-49), not 90 and 00. Same repro as 1985-GR-VII.1.3.5-5.

adjudication.reason: An OPEN refused with status 90 (LINAGE of zero) leaves the file open: a second OPEN gives 41, a WRITE 90, the CLOSE 00. At 1985 a 9x statement is unsuccessful, so the WRITE is 48 and the CLOSE 42. The 2023 continuation (kb/Work PB526) is applied at every edition. Checker's confidence: medium-high.
